title: Operations, constituents and coinvariants
statement:
For Weil representations of [sk-d-real-weil], use the ordinary direct sum of [sk-d-linear],
diagonal tensor action, exterior action on $\bigwedge^r V$, dual action
$(g\lambda)(v)=\lambda(g^{-1}v)$, and determinant
$\det V=\bigwedge^{\dim V}V$. An irreducible representation is nonzero
with no proper nonzero invariant subspace. A constituent of $V$ is an
irreducible representation isomorphic to a subquotient $M/N$ of $V$,
for invariant subspaces $N\subseteq M\subseteq V$. For finite-dimensional
$V$ these are the irreducible successive quotients of a composition
series of [def-mg-weil-composition-series]; counted with multiplicity, their direct sum is a
semisimplification in the sense of [def-mg-weil-semisimplification].
For a subgroup $I$, set
$V^I=\{v:gv=v\text{ for all }g\in I\}$ and
$V_I=V/\langle gv-v:g\in I,v\in V\rangle$.
For $b\in\Qlb^\times$, the constant Weil line $B_b$ has action
$g\mapsto b^{\deg g}$. The Tate line is $\Qlb(n)=B_{q^{-n}}$.

proof.text: The direct-sum, tensor, exterior and top-exterior actions are the representation constructions of [sk-d-linear], specialized to the Weil group and coefficient field of [sk-d-real-weil]. For the dual, define gλ by v ↦ λ(g⁻¹v). This is linear, the identity acts trivially, and (g(hλ))(v)=λ(h⁻¹g⁻¹v)=((gh)λ)(v), so it defines the stated dual representation. The condition on irreducibility is precisely simplicity in [sk-d-linear].

proof.text: For finite-dimensional V, [lem-mg-composition-series-exists] supplies a composition series when V is nonzero; for V=0 take the length-zero series, which has no factors or irreducible subquotients. Each successive quotient is an irreducible subquotient by [def-mg-weil-composition-series]. Conversely let N⊆M⊆V have irreducible quotient M/N. Apply [lem-mg-composition-series-exists] to N and V/M, using the empty series when either is zero. Regard the series of N as subspaces of V, append M, and append the inverse images in V of the positive terms of the series of V/M. This is a composition series of V: the appended N⊂M has the given simple quotient, and if A⊂B are adjacent terms of the series of V/M, the map (π⁻¹B)/(π⁻¹A)→B/A sending [v] to [π(v)] is equivariant, onto, and injective since π(v)∈A exactly when v∈π⁻¹A. Here π:V→V/M is the quotient map. Thus every factor in the concatenation is simple. By [lem-mg-jordan-holder], this series and any chosen series of V have isomorphic factors with multiplicity. Hence M/N occurs among the factors of every chosen series. The direct sum retaining all these factors is exactly [def-mg-weil-semisimplification], and by [lem-mg-semisimplification-independent] the sums obtained from different composition series are isomorphic Weil representations.

proof.text: The displayed fixed-vector set V^I is a subspace: each g fixes zero and fixes sums and scalar multiples of fixed vectors because its action is linear. In V_I the brackets mean the linear span over the coefficient field, so the displayed quotient is an ordinary vector-space quotient. No normality of I is required for these two vector spaces, and no action of the whole Weil group on them is asserted.

source.place: Operations, constituents and coinvariants: displayed definitions and finite-dimensional constituent clause

proof.text: By [sk-d-real-weil], deg(gh)=deg(g)+deg(h) and deg(1)=0. On the underlying one-dimensional space Q̄_ℓ define g·z=b^{deg(g)}z. Since b is nonzero, integer powers are defined and nonzero, and b^{deg(gh)}=b^{deg(g)}b^{deg(h)}; this is a representation. On ker(deg) it is the identity, hence its geometric restriction is continuous. The scalar q is nonzero in the characteristic-zero coefficient field, so the substitution b=q^{-n} defines the Tate line for every integer n, with degree-one geometric Frobenius acting by q^{-n}.
